literal: Those who die without failing what they vowed, who indeed are those who can reprove their failure?
translation: Who is there that can reprove as a failure the death of those heroes who die without failing to fulfill what they vowed?
modern: தாங்கள் சபதம் செய்ததை தவறாமல் நிறைவேற்றுவதற்காக உயிரை விடுபவர்களை, அவர்கள் அடைந்த தோல்விக்காக யாரால் குற்றம் சொல்ல முடியும்?
explanation: This couplet praises the glorious death of warriors who remain true to their vows. When a warrior vows to achieve a heroic deed and dies in the battlefield without retreating or failing his word, his death is a supreme victory of honor. Even if he did not technically achieve the physical objective, no one can mock or reprove him for 'failing,' because he kept his vow unto death. The poet uses the word 'இழைத்தது' to mean 'that which was resolved or vowed' and 'ஒறுக்கிற்பவர்' to mean 'those who can find fault or punish,' highlighting that true honor lies in steadfastness to one's word rather than mere physical survival.
